task: Build a delisting-aware equity universe so a clean PASS becomes nameable -- SOURCE PROBE
question: Can any data source available in this repo return price history for tickers that have stopped trading during or after the measurement window?
method: Downloaded a fixed probe set of 14 tickers from yfinance (the repo's only free equity source) over 2021-11-01..2026-11-20: 12 that genuinely stopped trading in or after the window, plus 2 known survivors as controls. A delisting-aware universe requires the 12; if they cannot be fetched, no such universe can be built here.

probe_results.note: 89 bars starting 2026-07-17 is a different issuer reusing the symbol; using it would inject a fabricated history

why_this_matters: The 44-name point-in-time universe meets the pod's 22-name count bar but contains only survivors. Survivorship bias direction is UPWARD: names that died are absent, so a momentum strategy's winners are kept and its losers are deleted from the sample. That inflates any measured edge, so a PASS on such a universe is not admissible evidence. This probe shows the repo cannot fix that by adding the missing names.

sources_checked.evidence: all 12 delisted probe tickers return 0 bars
no API key present for any of them (already recorded as COMS ask A1)

what_would_unblock_a_clean_PASS: A delisting-aware price source: CRSP (academic), Norgate Data (US delisted included), Polygon.io with delisted tickers, or Tiingo. Any one of them, keyed, would let tools/pit_equity_universe.py build a universe whose membership includes names that later died, at which point the survivorship flag can be removed honestly rather than by relabelling.
what_was_NOT_done_and_why: I did not fabricate a delisting-aware universe by injecting synthetic terminal losses for names that never existed in the data. A simulated death rate is a sensitivity test, and it may be worth running later, but it is not a replacement universe and must never be labelled one: the whole purpose of the flag is to stop exactly that kind of relabelling.
consequence: The H-201 pod's verdict stays capped at CANDIDATE_SURVIVORSHIP_FLAGGED. The count bar is met; the purpose of the bar is not. A KILL remains admissible, because failing to clear zero despite upward bias is the stronger result.
